coverage: Verified candidate file sha256 hashes against the packet (schematic, PCB, requirements).

Manually traced schematic wire/label/pin geometry for R1, C1, J1 (including J1's 180-degree rotation) and confirmed it matches the exported netlist: /IN={J1.1,R1.1}, /OUT={C1.1,J1.2,R1.2}, GND={C1.2,J1.3}.
Cross-checked PCB pad net assignments and track/via/zone connectivity against the schematic netlist (geometry probe output and DRC schematic parity = 0).
Reviewed fresh ERC (0 violations), DRC (0 violations, 0 unconnected, 0 parity issues), netlist and geometry check outputs.

Evaluated the stated shutdown criterion analytically (tau = R1*C1 = 10 ms; v(5ms) = e^-0.5 = 0.6065 V) and confirmed with an ngspice-42 transient simulation using the verified topology and stated initial conditions (ic=1 V on C1, /IN grounded, no external load).

Checked startup/bias trivially satisfied: purely passive network, no bias, reset, or brownout circuitry present; interface is a 3-pin header carrying /IN, /OUT, GND consistently between schematic and board.

findings.mechanism: With /IN grounded, the only discharge path for C1 is through R1, giving tau = 100 kOhm x 100 nF = 10 ms. Meeting 0.01 V (a factor of 100 decay) at 5 ms requires tau <= 5 ms / ln(100) = 1.086 ms. The saved values leave /OUT at 1 V x e^(-0.5) = 0.6065 V at 5 ms, about 61x above the limit; the node would not reach 0.01 V until tau x ln(100) = 46.05 ms.
findings.reasoning: The topology and connectivity are correct (verified by manual pin-geometry trace of the schematic, the kicad-cli netlist export, PCB pad nets, and DRC schematic parity = 0), so the failure is purely the saved component values. Both the closed-form solution of the first-order RC discharge and an ngspice transient with the stated initial condition agree to six significant figures that /OUT = 0.6065 V at 5 ms, versus the 0.01 V limit. This is the only functional criterion the packet states, and it is missed by a factor of ~61, so the defect is blocking. ERC/DRC passing does not bear on this electrical requirement. Grounding /IN through any non-zero source impedance would only make the result worse, so the ideal-ground assumption is conservative in the design's favor.
findings.title: R1*C1 discharge time constant ~9.2x too large: /OUT is 0.607 V at 5 ms, violating the 0.01 V shutdown requirement

limitations: Simulation used ideal R and C per the stated scope; PCB parasitics (trace resistance/capacitance) were not extracted, but at 100 kOhm / 100 nF scale they are negligible and could not change the ~61x criterion miss.
'/IN grounded at t=0' was modeled as an ideal zero-impedance ground on the /IN node; any real source impedance would only slow the discharge, making the result conservative in the design's favor.
Component tolerances were not evaluated (scope specifies saved values and ideal passives).
Zone fill was evaluated as saved (read-only candidate); no refill pass was performed, consistent with the packet's DRC limitation note.
